trajectory.text: I’ll start with the required single action, then check the bot state and build from the first result.
The bot is connected at the starter area with 15 Mind runes and 25 Air runes. I’m checking the API and local Magic notes while I test one spell so we can get a real baseline quickly.
Wind Strike landed for 237 raw XP. I’ll spend the starter runes against nearby rats and men in a fast target-switching loop, then compare the next sampled window.

The first spell burst scored 47 normalized XP/min. I found the nearby men yield coins through pickpocketing, and Aubury’s Varrock shop sells Air and Mind runes; I’m funding a refill so the Magic burst can continue.
Curse gives 725 raw XP per cast and can be recast on the same rat, so it beats the starter spell for the sample. I’m using the remaining Earth runes now, then I’ll restock and repeat the best loop.

Curse is confirmed at 725 raw XP per successful cast; missed attempts leave runes untouched. The target’s movement caused some misses, so I’m earning enough coins for a larger supply batch, then I’ll run a loop that reselects reachable targets before each cast.

The Curse loop reached 145 XP/min, with 10 successful casts inside one sample and 12 total. I’m improving target stability next: nearby rats die or wander, so I’ll test repeated casts on a higher HP cow after restocking.

The guard test was too dangerous: the guards killed the character and the inventory was lost. The score is still 145 XP/min, and I’ve respawned in Lumbridge. I’m rebuilding a smaller Curse supply and will stay on cows, which were much safer.

Wind Blast delivered 688 raw XP per cast versus Curse’s 725, and it costs more runes. Curse remains the better choice. Earth Blast is still level-locked at 51; I’m converting the unused Death runes back into the Curse runes and returning to the cow field.

I’ve confirmed why recent casts were missed: retargeting cows during active combat caused refusals. Waiting briefly between Curse casts kept a target stable and produced nine successful casts in 12 seconds. I’m funding one final larger batch to try to beat the 145 XP/min peak.
I’m at Magic 58 with the benchmark’s peak still 145 XP/min. The last Curse batch added seven casts but didn’t beat the earlier 10-cast window; I’m letting the final 15-second sample close.

**Peak score: 145 real-game XP/min**, from 7,250 raw Magic XP in one 15-second window.

Magic reached level 58 (60,125 XP). Wind Strike peaked at 47 XP/min; Curse was the best approach at 725 raw XP per successful cast. Wind Blast gave 688, and Earth Blast was still level-locked at Magic 51. I funded rune refills through guard pickpocketing and trained on cows. One guard-combat attempt ended in a death, so I switched to the safer cow field.

I’ll check the bot’s current state, read the available Bot/SDK references, and make the requested one-action tutorial call first. Then I’ll try Prayer training methods in short iterations and track the fixed-window peak rate.

The bot is connected and Prayer is still level 1 with 0 XP. I’m checking the action reference and Prayer-specific local notes now, then I’ll test the most direct bone/altar route available from the current position.

The initial rats here do not drop bones, so I’m switching to bone-dropping NPCs. The SDK reference confirms the direct route is to pick up bones and use their inventory “Bury” action. I’m checking for nearby drops after combat, then I’ll settle on the fastest repeatable loop.

We have a working baseline: burying regular bones gives 112 raw Prayer XP each, and the current Lumbridge woman loop has reached a 4 XP/min normalized peak. I’m testing a low-HP chicken area next; its bone drops may support faster 15-second bursts.

The chicken method supplies about 10 bones/minute. Bones stack in this server, and burying a 10-bone stack took 4.5 seconds, so I’m building a larger stack and will try a concentrated burst against the benchmark’s 15-second windows.
The batch is still farming successfully; I’m letting it fill the inventory stack so we can test whether a larger burial burst raises the sampled peak.
The stack is still accumulating. Once it reaches capacity, I’ll bury the whole stack quickly and check whether the benchmark records the burst.
The fill rate is slower than the 10-bone trial, so I’m watching the loop’s 3-minute cap. Even a partial stack should still let us measure the burst method.
The larger burial burst was recorded at 25 XP/min, with 1,237 raw XP in its best window. I’m repeating the fill-and-burst cycle and will try to fit the whole stack inside one aligned sample window.
The second stack is building at the chicken spawn. The approach is producing steady Prayer XP without needing to travel between kills.
The fill phase is taking roughly three minutes per 26-bone stack. The next burial phase should finish in about 11 seconds; I’m keeping the farming method running for the remaining benchmark time.

The previous 26-bone burial crossed a sample boundary, splitting its XP across two windows (25 and 34 XP/min). The next window has just begun with the stack ready, so I’m burying it immediately to keep the XP inside one 15-second sample.
The aligned attempt scored 38 XP/min, an improvement. I’m continuing the same chicken-and-bone cycle and will use the next stack to push that peak higher while accumulating Prayer XP.
The next inventory is filling. I’ll keep monitoring the tracker between cycles so the final score reflects its last completed windows.
The farm remains stable; it takes around three minutes to collect a full stack. The player has leveled combat along the way, which should help maintain the kill rate.

I switched the bronze sword to its aggressive Strength style to see whether higher hit damage improves bone collection. I’m testing that on the next stack; burial speed and XP per bone remain unchanged.
The Strength-style trial is still collecting. I’ll compare its kills and pickups to the earlier 26-bone runs, then bury the stack.

The last burial crossed another sample edge, but the overall peak remains 56 XP/min. I’ll collect one more full stack, then use continuous chicken kills and burials for the remaining time after the next burst.

The final full-stack run is underway. Aggressive style is still active; if the inventory fills early, I’ll move straight to the burial and finish training rather than waste the remaining minutes on another long fill.
That burial brought Prayer to level 40 and 16,875 XP. Five minutes remain, so I’m collecting one more stack for a final burst, then I’ll spend the remaining time on steady XP.
The final stack is filling at the established rate. I’ll monitor the remaining time and switch to direct pickup-and-bury as soon as the last burst is done.
Three minutes remain. The current peak is still 56 XP/min; I’m using the remaining time to gather and bury one final stack, then I’ll check the completed benchmark score.
The final collection is progressing normally. I’ll use whatever stack is ready for the last burial and stay within the benchmark’s remaining time.

The final aligned stack produced the best window: 2,925 raw XP over 15 seconds, scoring 59 XP/min. One minute remains, so I’m continuing the faster continuous kill, pickup, and bury loop to finish the full training interval.

Prayer training finished at **level 45 with 24,075 XP**. The peak score was **61 XP/min**, from the **29:15–29:30** sample window.

Chickens provided bones; burying a full inventory produced the strongest bursts. I dropped basic starter gear and runes to make room for the bones.
I’ll make the requested one-action baseline call first, then check the live state and iterate on the fastest Thieving method available.

The character is at Lumbridge castle with several reachable men. The project notes say this is a proven level 1 start; I’m checking the exact interaction pattern and then I’ll measure a short run before committing the 30-minute loop.

The high-level helper timed out before starting the attempt, while the direct SDK interaction did trigger a real attempt. I’ll use the direct pickpocket option with short waits and live XP checks; the first attempt failed and stunned the character, so the short loop will also show the actual attempt cadence.

The direct loop is working: it gained 10,000 raw Thieving XP in 20 seconds, with a 148 real-game XP/min peak so far. At level 33, warriors are available, so I’m testing whether the higher-XP target beats the nearby men after travel time.
The walk to Al Kharid hasn’t returned yet, so I’m not letting that route stall the session. I’m checking whether it completes; if it remains blocked, I’ll resume the nearby pickpocket loop.
I found the delay: the Al Kharid gate requires accepting the 10 gp toll. That choice is now made, so I’m crossing and will compare the warrior XP rate directly against the nearby-men baseline.

The farmer loop produced 9,425 raw XP in 20 seconds, below the nearby men’s measured pace, and repeated stun messages explain the lost time. I’m back at the men and will keep the higher measured method running with brief stun recovery, then check the fixed-window score.

Men remain the best tested target: the latest 20-second run gained 9,800 raw XP and reached level 48. I’m testing a tighter one-tick dispatch cadence briefly; if the server rejects or drops the extra attempts, I’ll return to the two-tick loop for the rest of the benchmark.
The faster cadence set a new peak of 168 XP/min. I’m keeping it in short, monitored batches so the benchmark continues to sample without risking a long uncontrolled run.

The faster loop raised the peak to 200 XP/min. The character died once during the run and respawned nearby, but Thieving XP persisted; I’m recovering the dropped food now so future stun damage is less likely to interrupt the run.
The one-tick loop is now at level 65 and the measured peak has climbed to 248 XP/min. I’ll keep that cadence; the only interruption so far was one respawn, with Thieving XP retained.

I got through the toll gate and reached the Al Kharid warriors. This is the higher-level target I wanted to compare; I’m measuring a 15-second one-tick loop before deciding whether to stay here or return to the faster men.

The warrior test is clearly faster: it added 21,450 raw XP in 15 seconds and lifted the peak to 403 XP/min. The warrior hit hard enough to kill the character and respawn it in Lumbridge, so I’m checking whether I can resume there without repeating the toll.

The return walk is taking longer than the first trip because the toll gate state is uncertain after death. I’ll stop spending time on that route if it can’t pass promptly and keep training at the reachable Lumbridge targets.

The toll cost is consumed, and the return attempt after death would need another 10 gp, so I’ve returned to the nearby men rather than repeat a risky detour. The warrior window already secured the 403 XP/min peak; I’m continuing Thieving locally for the remaining time.

The return path completed in the background and the character is back among the warriors. I’m taking another short warrior sample at the higher Thieving level; after that I’ll keep the strongest practical loop running through the benchmark’s remaining time.

Warriors still produce the best single-window score, but each attempt ends in a respawn within roughly 12 seconds, and the return trip would consume most of the remaining time. I’m switching back to the nearby men for steady XP while preserving the 403 XP/min peak already recorded.
At Thieving level 70, the character is back at the Lumbridge men. I’m using the rapid direct interaction loop for this steady stretch; the benchmark’s fixed-window peak remains 403 XP/min.

The warrior method with kebab healing produced 442 XP/min, the new peak, and sustained a full 30-second run without dying. I’ve used the bought kebabs, so I’m taking another short high-level sample before finishing the remaining benchmark time.

The warrior loop now raised the peak to 845 XP/min. It ended with another death and a Lumbridge respawn, so I’m finishing the remaining 75 seconds at the immediately available men rather than spending time on another food trip.

**Peak score: 845 real-game XP/min**, from 42,250 raw XP in the 15-second window at 28:30–28:45.

I trained Thieving to **level 87 (465,025 XP)** over the 30-minute run. Lumbridge men were steady, but Al Kharid warriors with kebab healing produced the highest rate.
I’ll start with the required one-action tutorial skip, then check the character state and move straight into a short fishing attempt.

The tutorial skip completed and the net is in inventory. The character is still in the starting area, so I’m locating the nearest net fishing spot and will test a single fishing interaction before committing to a loop.
The Draynor net spot is working. I’m switching to repeated Net interactions and will check the fixed-window score shortly; then I’ll keep fishing there while clearing inventory as needed.

We’ve found a strong baseline: the bot reached Fishing 36 and the peak window is 115 real-game XP/min. I’ve freed the inventory for fishing; I’m checking whether the nearby shop route offers a faster method, then I’ll spend the remaining time on the best working setup.

A 200 ms click cadence raised production substantially; 100 ms spam nearly stopped catches, so I’m settling back on 200 ms. I’m running that cadence with automatic inventory clearing and level-up dismissal, then I’ll compare the measured windows.
The sustained run is still active. It’s holding the character at the Draynor net spots and periodically freeing caught fish so the inventory won’t stop the skill loop.
The 200 ms loop has pushed the peak to 305 XP/min. I’m trying a slightly faster 175 ms cadence for a short comparison; if catches slow down, I’ll return to the proven interval.

The faster 175 ms cadence averages a little higher, though the best window remains 305 XP/min. Since this spot only yields shrimp and anchovies, I’m going to test fly fishing for higher XP fish; the current catch inventory should cover the rod and feathers at Gerrant’s shop.

Fly fishing raised the peak again to 725 XP/min, and the character is now Fishing 80. I’m keeping this method and have enough feathers for another test; I’ll probe one slightly faster cadence before settling into the remaining training time.
I restocked the fly rod with another 183 feathers; the supply should support roughly two minutes at the current catch pace. I’m continuing at 175 ms and keeping the inventory cleared.
The 90 second fly fishing block is still running; it is using the Lure spots and dismissing level dialogs while dropping excess trout and salmon.
The peak is now 730 XP/min. I’m keeping fly fishing as the best method and cycling fish sales into more feathers so training can continue through the remaining time.
There are about eight benchmark minutes left. I’m running another two minute fly fishing block; the 323 feathers should leave enough for a final stocked loop and one last score check.
The two minute block is still in progress and the inventory cleanup loop is active, so catches aren’t being blocked by a full bag.
The last high volume block is underway. There are four and a half benchmark minutes remaining; I’ll keep the bot fishing through the cutoff and report the final peak.
The benchmark has two minutes left. I’ve restocked with 183 feathers and am returning to the Barbarian Village spots for the final fly fishing block.
The final training block remains active at the established 175 ms cadence. It should finish with time for a last score check before the benchmark window closes.

Completed the 30-minute Fishing run. **Peak score: 820 real-game XP/min**, measured over the 15-second window from 22:15 to 22:30.

Fishing reached level 99 with 1,350,250 XP. Fly fishing trout and salmon at Barbarian Village, using the 175 ms interaction cadence, beat net fishing at Draynor.
I’ll check the bot’s current state and the exact MCP method names, then make the requested one-action tutorial call and start measuring Attack XP.

The bot is in-game at the tutorial area, with Attack 10 and an unarmed combat style. I’m checking the combat and equipment API now, then I’ll switch to the strongest available Attack-training setup and measure a short baseline.

The Attack baseline works: one low level rat kill added 200 raw XP, but that target is only 2 HP, so I’m moving to a denser, higher HP spawn. I’ve equipped the bronze sword and confirmed its accurate style trains Attack.

The cow field is accessible through the opened gate. A cow kill gave 800 raw Attack XP, substantially better than the rat, and the character still has 17 HP. I’m running a short cow rotation now, with food use and automatic dialog handling, then I’ll compare the 15 second score samples.

The cow rotation added 4,900 raw XP in 45 seconds with no healing needed; Attack rose to 29. The benchmark currently shows a peak of 32 real-game XP/min. I’m tightening target selection to nearby unengaged cows and will compare that against the current rotation before settling into the remaining run.

The nearby only-target selection raised the peak to 34 XP/min and added 5,000 raw XP in 45 seconds. Attack is now 36. I’m going to test Al-Kharid warriors briefly: the denser, higher HP targets may sustain combat with less respawn downtime, though they could hit harder.

The path to Al-Kharid is taking longer than the local cow loop, so travel cost may outweigh any gain from stronger targets. I’m letting the route finish and will use only a short sample there before deciding whether to return.
Goblins were slower: 2,600 raw XP in 35 seconds, with the benchmark’s recent rate at 22 XP/min. I’m returning to the cow pen; its 34 XP/min peak remains the best approach so far.

The Al-Kharid trip attempt was cut off before reaching the warriors, and the bot stayed near the goblin area. I’m back in the cow field now, running a longer sample at Attack 39 with nearby-target filtering and food checks.

The two minute cow sample added 13,200 raw XP and kept the recent rate at 34 XP/min, with HP stable. Four target attempts failed, likely because some nearby cows were unreachable, so I’m excluding unreachable cows to reduce wasted interactions.

Excluding unreachable cows improved the best fixed window to 38 XP/min (1,900 raw XP per 15 seconds). The bot is still fighting safely in the pen, so I’m keeping this filter through the sample and will use the remaining time to keep the best setup running.

That three minute cow run added 20,000 raw XP, averaged about 33 normalized XP/min, and needed no food. The peak remains 38. I’m continuing on cows with the reachability filter; goblins and the attempted warrior route were worse.
The filtered cow loop is holding recent samples around 32–36 XP/min. I’m continuing the same setup; the peak window is still 38 XP/min at the 10 minute mark.

The benchmark is at 17½ of 30 minutes. This cow rotation’s recent window is back up to 36 XP/min, with the historical peak at 38; Attack is already 60. I’m continuing the proven rotation until the full benchmark period completes.

The last three minute run added 19,900 raw XP, with HP at 49 and no food used. The bot is still in the cow pen, and the 38 XP/min peak is unchanged. I’m extending the same reliable rotation for the remaining benchmark time.

The current ten minute rotation is progressing steadily; recent windows remain around 34 XP/min, and no healing has been needed. The best sample is still 38 XP/min. I’ll keep it running through the remaining benchmark window.

The peak remains 38 XP/min, and recent samples are 32–34. Attack is now well above the weapon unlock threshold, but the character has no stronger weapon available; staying on the low defense cows keeps the XP flow consistent.

A new fixed sample at 23:15–23:30 raised the peak to 40 XP/min (2,000 raw XP over 15 seconds). The current samples are also at 40, so I’m keeping the setup unchanged through the remaining six minutes.
Attack has reached 70, HP is 55, and the cow loop is still active without food use. The benchmark has 3:15 left; peak remains 40 XP/min.
The benchmark is at 29:15 of 30:00, still peaking at 40 XP/min. I’m letting the final sample window finish, then I’ll report the score and final Attack XP.

Completed the 30 minute Attack run. Peak score: **40 real-game XP/min**, from 2,000 raw XP in the 15 second window at 23:15–23:30.

Attack rose from level 10 (980 XP) to level 72 (155,680 XP). Cows with the bronze sword’s accurate style gave the best rate; goblins were slower.
I’ll start with the required single tutorial action, then check the bot’s state and build from the first Crafting XP result.

The bot is connected at level 1 Crafting with starter supplies. I’m checking the SDK references and local Crafting guides now, then I’ll try the fastest actionable method with the items and location available.

The world-state dump shows Lumbridge and a furnace plus bank across town, but no starting Crafting materials. The first attempt to path to the bank is taking too long, so I’m stopping that route and will use an immediate local training option instead.

The rate checker confirms 0 XP so far, with about 27 minutes left. My bank trip opened a guard dialog and stopped south of the Al Kharid gate; I’ve identified this as a navigation snag and am checking the nearby crafting supplies and shops before choosing a loop.

I’ve reached 12 coins by pickpocketing, enough for the Al Kharid toll and the two basic leather tools. I’m going through the gate next, then I’ll source hides, tan them, and test the leather crafting action for actual XP before committing to a loop.

The tools are purchased and I have 3 coins left. The route to the Lumbridge cow pen is getting stuck in pathfinding, so I’m checking the live position and will reroute through nearby waypoints or use a local source of hides.

I’ve collected the first cow hide. The route between the Lumbridge pen and Al Kharid tannery is the main bottleneck, so I’m letting this one route attempt resolve while tracking the benchmark clock; once I reach the tanner, I can verify Crafting XP and optimize around the actual action time.

The first leather glove produced 345 raw Crafting XP and raised Crafting to level 4. I’ve confirmed Al Kharid tanning works; I’m switching to stocking hides and doing a concentrated crafting batch, which is where the 15-second score window can improve.

The boot batch raised Crafting to level 20. The tracker hasn’t registered a higher peak yet, so I’m using the remaining time for one more stocked batch and will check the fixed-window score after it lands.

Crafting reached **level 25** with 4,985 XP. The peak score was **33 real-game XP/min**, measured at 1,630 raw XP in one 15-second window.

I used tanned leather to craft gloves and boots; boots produced more XP per item. The benchmark ended at 30m 15s, 15 seconds past the requested limit.
I’m starting with the required single tutorial-skip action, then I’ll check the bot’s state and get a Mining baseline before iterating.
The bot is in-game with a bronze pickaxe and Mining level 1. I’m locating nearby mineable rocks and confirming the interaction API, then I’ll test one mining action.
I reached the southeast Varrock mine; copper, tin, and iron are all within a few tiles. I’ll establish XP on copper first, then switch to the fastest ore the level allows.

The first copper ore produced 437 raw XP (level 5), confirming a useful baseline. I’m testing a short loop that rotates among nearby copper and tin rocks and clears ore only when the inventory needs space; then I’ll keep the best method running and monitor the benchmark samples.

Rotating across distinct rocks raised the Mining benchmark peak from 18 to 228 XP/min, and the bot is now level 44. I’m keeping the pickaxe on iron rocks and will drop mined ore before the inventory fills, checking the fixed-window score as it runs.

The unattended iron cycle is working: Mining is level 63, and the fixed-window peak has climbed to 280 XP/min. The bot is still collecting ore and clearing its inventory as needed; I’m letting the run continue.

The long-run execute call hit the MCP client’s 300-second wait limit, but the server-side code kept running: the character is Mining 84 with 363,562 raw XP. Benchmark time is 10:45, and the peak remains 280 XP/min.

The score has stabilized at 280 XP/min while the bot keeps gaining Mining levels and the inventory remains under control. Since iron is producing a steady peak, I’m maintaining this cycle through most of the benchmark and will use the final minutes for one more speed comparison if time allows.
At 20 minutes, the character is Mining 96 with 861,437 raw XP. Recent 15-second windows fluctuate between 263 and 280 XP/min; the best remains 280. The iron cycle is still active.

The iron loop has carried Mining to level 99 and 1.21 million raw XP. The peak is still 280 XP/min; the current run has about a minute left, after which I’ll test gold briefly before the 30-minute benchmark ends.

The brief gold comparison failed because Al Kharid scorpions killed the character during travel, so the bot respawned in Lumbridge and lost the pickaxe. The 280 XP/min peak is preserved. I’m restoring a bronze pickaxe and returning to safe iron rocks for the remaining benchmark time.

Mining benchmark completed at 30:00. **Peak: 280 real-game XP/min**, from 14,000 raw XP in the 15-second window at 13:00–13:15. The character reached Mining 99 with 1,275,312 raw XP.

Rotating through Varrock iron rocks produced the best rate. A late gold-ore test ended with the character dying to scorpions; the peak score was preserved, but the character is now back near Varrock without a pickaxe.
I’m starting with the required single tutorial-skip action, then I’ll check the bot’s state and get a first Cooking attempt running.
The bot is connected at Cooking 1 with starter gear and no raw fish. I’m checking the available interaction methods and nearby fishing/cooking spots, then I’ll establish a short baseline.

I found a chicken coop only about 75 tiles from the start, with multiple level 1 chickens. That should supply raw meat faster than travelling to a fishing area; I’m switching to sword kills and checking the first drop.

Cooking worked on the Lumbridge range: the first successful chicken gave 750 raw XP and reached level 8. The nearby fire source burned the first attempt, so I’m using the range and now testing a batch method to keep the 15-second XP windows full.

The batch method reached Cooking 37 and produced a 90 XP/min peak, with one burn in the 10-chicken batch. I’m testing whether leveling Fishing to fly-fishing range can raise the cooking XP per item enough to beat the chicken loop.

The fishing trial has reached Fishing 39 and unlocked trout/salmon; the higher-value catch is promising. I’m checking for a range near the river before deciding whether this is faster than the proven chicken batch.

The nearby Range at (3097, 3367) is reachable and cuts the fly-fishing route to about 70 tiles. I’m filling one 18-fish inventory there, then cooking it in one continuous range batch so a single sample window captures as much XP as possible.

The 18-fish run set a 645 XP/min peak (32,250 raw XP in one aligned window). I’m using the chickens’ feather drops to restock the fly rod cheaply, then I’ll try a larger fish batch to push that peak higher.

The second fish cycle maintained 825 XP/min, and I have a final inventory of 20 raw fish ready. I’m adding a few more catches before one last timed cook batch; the benchmark has about 90 seconds remaining.

**30-minute run complete. Peak score: 825 real-game XP/min**, from a 15-second window with 41,250 raw Cooking XP.

Fly-fishing trout and salmon, then cooking them in batches on the reachable range, beat the chicken method. Cooking reached level 77 (225,250 raw XP). The nearby fire burned food more often, so I used ranges for cooking.
I’m checking the available RS-Agent controls, then I’ll send the requested one-action tutorial skip and start a short baseline.

Tutorial skip connected successfully. The character is unarmed, Defence 15, and surrounded by level 1 rats; I’m checking the combat controls and nearby training options before the first short Defence run.

The defensive style is active, but the initial rat window scored only 4 real XP/min. I’m moving to the nearby cow field to test a denser, higher-HP target supply and will compare its next aligned samples.

The cow-field loop has sustained roughly 34–38 normalized XP/min and raised Defence to 35 without meaningful HP loss. I’m testing Al-Kharid warriors next; their higher HP may improve XP per kill, though I’ll switch back if hit rate drops.
The walk to Al-Kharid is taking longer than expected, likely due to the route or gate pathing. I’m letting this bounded navigation call resolve before choosing the next target.
That route stopped at the Al-Kharid border with a blocking guard dialog, so the warrior test did not start. I’m clearing the dialog and trying the nearby goblin cluster as the next comparison.

The Al-Kharid route proved obstructed by the toll dialogue, so I’m staying at the cow field. I’m testing faster low-level target dispatch now; the last loop spent measurable time reacquiring targets after kills.

The warrior test was worse: one sustained fight lowered HP, and I died while leaving Al-Kharid. The gear is intact in inventory; I’m re-equipping the sword and shield and returning to the safer cow field for the remaining benchmark time.

Direct SDK target dispatch improved the peak to **112 real XP/min** at the 12:00–12:15 sample. I’m keeping that cow-field loop running, with checks for Defence style and equipment, and will monitor the fixed 15-second score windows.
The current run is holding around 102–116 XP/min, with the 116 peak still leading. The cow loop is safe at this Defence level, so I’m continuing it through the remaining benchmark window.

The longer control call reached the client’s 300-second wait cap, which can outlast the reply while the in-game script completes. I’m checking the score and bot state, then I’ll resume a short loop for the remaining benchmark time.

The direct cow loop is still producing over 100 XP/min in recent samples, and the character has progressed well beyond Defence 68. The benchmark has 8½ minutes left; I’m keeping the same reliable method active.

Defence is now 76, and the active four-minute run dispatched 189 cow attacks without errors. I’m using one short chicken-field comparison to see whether quicker kills improve the peak; then I’ll spend the remaining time on whichever area scores better.
The chicken test gave about 79 normalized XP/min over 45 seconds, below the cow loop’s roughly 99 average and 116 peak. I’m returning to cows and continuing there through the final five minutes.
The run is at 28:00 with the peak still 116 XP/min. Two benchmark minutes remain; I’m letting the cow loop finish out the scored period.

Completed the 30-minute Defence run. Peak score: **116 real XP/min**, from the 13:30–13:45 sample window.

The best method was a bronze sword and wooden shield on **Block** style, repeatedly attacking cows with direct target dispatch. Defence finished at **level 81** with **301,560 XP**. Rats, chickens, and Al-Kharid warriors were less effective; the warrior test ended in a death.
I’ll first check the bot’s state, then use one simple in-game action to get an initial Fletching baseline and iterate from there.

The bot is at the starting area with no fletching materials, so the first useful path is to get a knife and logs, then test bow fletching. I’m checking the available game API and local notes for a nearby source before committing to a longer loop.

The first fletch succeeded: one log made 15 arrow shafts for 187 raw Fletching XP. The knife and nearby trees make a repeatable loop possible; I’m checking the benchmark and the XP values before choosing between shaft batches and bows.

The opening batch did not sustain: the first tree interaction after the initial log timed out without producing a log. I’m adjusting the loop to verify each chop’s result before continuing, so the benchmark window only counts actual Fletching XP.

The tracker has a 4 XP/min peak from the initial shaft batch. Arrow shafts award about 188 raw XP per log here, so I’ll keep them as the main method and run a bounded woodcut-and-fletch loop, recovering from any failed chops.

The loop is producing steady XP. The tracker now shows a 41 XP/min peak (2,063 raw XP in one 15-second window), a strong improvement over the initial baseline. I’ll leave it running and keep monitoring the fixed-window score.

The training call hit the MCP client’s 300-second wait limit, so I’m checking whether its in-game loop continued after the client stopped waiting. The benchmark’s recent rate just went quiet, and I’ll restart with shorter monitored runs if it stopped.

The bot action layer appears wedged on a path to Bob, and the previous loop was also repeating failed chops after the character died and lost the axe. I’m clearing the stuck bot session now, then I’ll reconnect and use shorter, checked batches so a failed prerequisite doesn’t run unattended.

The long loop gained about 24,000 raw XP before the character died; it then lost the axe and knife, so the remaining loop is generating failed chops. Its server-side execution continued after the 300-second client wait expired, which is blocking new bot actions. The current benchmark peak remains 45 XP/min.
